body.en: *Life insurance* is a contract in which the insurer agrees to pay a fixed sum on the death of the insured or on the maturity of the policy, in return for premiums. It is a contract of assurance, not indemnity, because the event (death) is certain and only its timing is uncertain. Main policies: whole life (pays on death, whenever it happens), endowment (pays at maturity or on earlier death), and term insurance (pays only if death occurs within the term; lowest premium). It protects families, encourages saving and can be used as security for loans.

body.en: Life *insurance* covers human life, is a contract of assurance, is long-term and has a savings element. Fire insurance covers property against fire, is a contract of indemnity, usually runs for a year, and needs insurable interest both when the policy is taken and when the loss occurs. Marine insurance covers the ship, cargo and freight against the perils of the sea, is a contract of indemnity, and needs insurable interest at the time of loss. Other important types today include health, motor (third-party cover is compulsory by law) and crop insurance.

points.en: Fire: indemnity, one year, average clause
*Marine*: hull, cargo, freight; interest at loss

say.en: Stock worth 10 rupees lakh is insured for 6 rupees lakh with an average clause. A fire destroys stock worth 5 rupees lakh. Find the claim.
Proportion insured equals 6 divided by 10 equals 0.6.
Claim equals Loss times 0.6 equals 5 times 0.6 equals 3 rupees lakh.
The owner bears the remaining 2 rupees lakh as his own insurer for the uninsured part.
So the answer is 3 rupees lakh.
